items.title: Europe Is Adopting Vera, One Country at a Time. Italy Is the Latest
items.summary: Il Sole 24 Ore, Rassegna Business, and Sanità Digitale cover Vera Health's growth in Italy. The papers wrote "one in nine doctors"; the latest data already says one in six. And almost all of them arrived the same way: because a colleague showed them an answer.

items.title: Vera Health Accelerates Its Expansion in Spain: One in Seven Doctors Already Use Vera
items.summary: elEconomista and El Español each published a feature today on Vera Health's expansion in Spain, a market where one in seven doctors already uses the platform. Almost all of them arrived the same way: another doctor recommended it.

items.title: How AI is Quietly Transforming Mental Healthcare
items.summary: AI is taking on a growing role in mental healthcare, helping clinicians personalize treatment, monitor outcomes, and cut documentation time, according to a review in the Annual Review of Clinical Psychology.

items.title: The Next Blockbuster Drug May Already Exist, and AI Knows Where to Look
items.summary: AI can play a significant role in drug repurposing, identifying existing medicines that may work for new diseases, according to a review in the Annual Review of Medicine. Because these drugs are already approved, repurposing can be faster and cheaper than developing new ones.

items.title: Dedicated Module Useful in Helping Internal Physicians Interpret Ambulatory Blood Pressure Readings
items.summary: An asynchronous e-learning module sharply improved internal medicine residents' confidence in interpreting ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, according to a study in BMC Medical Education, where the share who felt comfortable rose from 22.6% to 84.6%.

items.title: Can AI Help Us Sleep Better? New Research Suggests It Can
items.summary: Research into AI in sleep medicine is yielding useful applications for insomnia, sleep-related breathing disorders, hypersomnolence, and parasomnias, according to a review in Respiratory Medicine, where AI is positioned to support rather than replace clinicians.

items.title: Korean Experts Make Series of Recommendations for Managing Acute Colonic Diverticulitis
items.summary: The Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases reached a Delphi consensus on diagnosing and managing acute colonic diverticulitis, offering region-specific, evidence-based guidance for a disease that is becoming more common in Asia.

items.title: Case Report: Management of Large Uterine Fibroids Causing Uterine Torsion During Delivery
items.summary: A 29-year-old primigravida at term with a giant uterine fibroid and a transverse fetal lie developed uterine torsion. This case report details how the surgical team prepared for multiple scenarios and safely delivered via a posterior lower uterine segment incision.

items.title: GLP-1 RAs Associated With Reduced Progression in Some Cancers
items.summary: A propensity-matched analysis of more than 10,000 patients across seven solid tumors found that GLP-1 receptor agonists were associated with reduced metastatic progression, reaching statistical significance in four cancers. The authors call for randomized trials.

items.title: Medical Students With Specific Learning Disabilities Continue to Face Educational Hurdles
items.summary: A mixed-methods systematic review in BMC Medical Education finds that extra time can level exam performance for medical students with specific learning disabilities, but accommodations alone leave real gaps. The authors call for a comprehensive, flexible approach, and AI tools may have a role.

items.title: Daraxonrasib Demonstrates Superiority Over Chemotherapy in Metastatic Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma
items.summary: In the phase 3 RASolute 302 study presented at ASCO 2026, the RAS(ON) inhibitor daraxonrasib nearly doubled median overall survival versus chemotherapy (13.2 vs 6.6 months) in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer, with far fewer treatment discontinuations.

items.title: Generative AI Tools Potentially Associated With a Decline in Medical Students' Mental Well-Being
items.summary: A new study in JMIR Medical Education finds that uncertainty about generative AI — including threats to professional identity and job security — may be contributing to a decline in medical students' mental well-being.

items.title: ACEP and Vera Health Partner to Deliver Trusted AI to Emergency Physicians
items.summary: The American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) and Vera Health, a clinical search engine that gives clinicians evidence-based answers to medical questions in seconds, today announced a partnership that brings ACEP's clinical policies directly into Vera's database.
